name: Automotive
summary: Lead response, service reminders, repair status texts, recall alerts, and trade-in follow-up.

automations.title: Lead Follow-Up & Test Drive Scheduling System
automations.summary: Every new internet lead (from the website, third-party listing sites, or ad campaigns) is immediately acknowledged with a personalized text and…
steps: Every new internet lead (from the website, third-party listing sites, or ad campaigns) is immediately acknowledged with a personalized text and email, entered into the CRM with a lead score, and assigned to the first available salesperson.
If the salesperson hasn't made contact within two hours, the manager receives an escalation alert.

Leads who engage are guided straight to a self-scheduling link for a test drive appointment, cutting the average time from inquiry to appointment and dramatically increasing the percentage of leads that ever reach the lot.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a dealership sales manager is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.

automations.title: Repair Order Status & Vehicle Ready Notification System
automations.summary: From the moment a vehicle is dropped off, the customer receives automated status updates at each stage of the repair process (vehicle received…
steps: From the moment a vehicle is dropped off, the customer receives automated status updates at each stage of the repair process (vehicle received, inspection complete with recommended services, repair in progress, and vehicle ready for pickup) all via text without the service advisor having to make a single phone call.

Vehicles that have been ready for more than four hours but haven't been picked up trigger a reminder text to the customer and a flag to the service advisor, keeping the service bay from becoming a parking lot.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a service advisor, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes.
tools: DMS (e.g., CDK Global or Reynolds & Reynolds)

automations.title: Maintenance Reminder & Lapsed Customer Win-Back System
automations.summary: Based on the mileage and service interval recorded at each visit, this automation calculates when each customer is due for their next oil change…
steps: Based on the mileage and service interval recorded at each visit, this automation calculates when each customer is due for their next oil change, tire rotation, or recommended service and sends a reminder text two weeks before that estimated date.
Customers who haven't returned in six months receive a win-back offer automatically, and any customer who leaves a negative review online is immediately flagged for a personal call from the owner.
The shop's relationship with every customer is actively managed even when the shop is buried in cars.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means an auto repair shop owner re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Shop-Ware or Tekmetric)

automations.title: Deal Paperwork Checklist & Funding Status Tracker
automations.summary: The moment a deal is desked, the system generates a complete checklist of every document required for that specific deal (based on the lender…
steps: The moment a deal is desked, the system generates a complete checklist of every document required for that specific deal (based on the lender, product mix, and customer type) and sends it to the F&I manager's deal queue.
As documents are received and uploaded, the checklist updates in real time, and the F&I manager knows exactly what's missing before they sit down with the customer.
After signing, the system tracks funding status with each lender and alerts the accounting office the moment a deal is funded and ready to post.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a finance & insurance manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving.
tools: Airtable or Google Sheets (deal checklist tracker)

automations.title: Fleet Renewal & Expansion Campaign System
automations.summary: Twelve months before the end of a fleet account's vehicle replacement cycle, the system automatically triggers an outreach sequence from the fleet…
steps: Twelve months before the end of a fleet account's vehicle replacement cycle, the system automatically triggers an outreach sequence from the fleet rep, a summary of the account's current vehicles, a preview of upcoming model changes, and a link to schedule a renewal consultation.
Fleet managers who engage receive a custom proposal generated from their account data; those who don't respond are re-queued for a phone call.
Between cycles, the fleet rep receives alerts when a tracked account adds employees, expands locations, or posts about growth, signals that a fleet expansion conversation is timely.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, a fleet sales representative has to notice problems after they've already happened, then scramble to fix them manually one at a time. None of it is difficult, it's just slow, repetitive, and easy to fall behind on.
tools: LinkedIn Sales Navigator or a news monitoring tool (expansion signals)

automations.title: Mileage-Based Service Reminder System
automations.summary: Using the mileage and date logged at each visit, this automation calculates when every customer is due for their next oil change, tire rotation, or…
steps: Using the mileage and date logged at each visit, this automation calculates when every customer is due for their next oil change, tire rotation, or manufacturer-recommended service interval, and sends a reminder text two to three weeks ahead of that date, timed off actual mileage patterns rather than a flat calendar interval.
Customers who don't respond within a week get a follow-up with a direct online booking link, cutting out the phone tag that eats up a service advisor's morning.
Shops that used to rely on customers remembering to call back in for their 5,000-mile service now see a steady, predictable stream of return visits instead of hoping people show up on their own.
automations.manualProcess: Left to a person, this means a service scheduler re-enters the same data more than once, double-checks it by hand, and still occasionally misses something.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Tekmetric or Shop-Ware)

automations.title: Diagnostic Approval & Pickup Alert Texts
automations.summary: Once a technician finishes the diagnostic scan, this automation texts the customer a link to a digital estimate broken down by recommended…
steps: Once a technician finishes the diagnostic scan, this automation texts the customer a link to a digital estimate broken down by recommended, required, and deferred repairs, letting them tap to approve or decline each line item from their phone instead of waiting on a callback from the service advisor.

Approved work is pushed straight back into the shop's work order automatically, and the moment the last approved item is signed off by the technician, the customer gets a ready-for-pickup text with the final invoice attached.
Estimate approval time drops from hours of phone tag to minutes, and the service advisor's desk phone stops ringing every ten minutes with "is it done yet" calls.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on an assistant service manager remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Tekmetric or Shop-Ware)

automations.title: VIN Recall Cross-Check & Notification
automations.summary: Once a week, this automation runs every customer VIN in the shop's database against the NHTSA recall API and manufacturer recall feeds, flagging any…
steps: Once a week, this automation runs every customer VIN in the shop's database against the NHTSA recall API and manufacturer recall feeds, flagging any vehicle with an open, unaddressed recall.

Affected customers are automatically sent a text and email explaining the specific recall in plain language, along with a link to book the repair, which for many recalls is performed at no cost to the customer.

What used to require someone manually checking VINs one at a time, or customers finding out about a recall only after an incident, now runs as a standing weekly check that keeps the shop ahead of safety issues and turns recall traffic into an opportunity to build trust instead of just processing a mandatory fix.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a warranty administrator manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Tekmetric or CDK Global)

automations.title: Trade-In Value Follow-Up Campaign
automations.summary: Using current market data (auction results, regional listing prices, and the dealership's own acquisition needs), this automation runs a monthly…
steps: Using current market data (auction results, regional listing prices, and the dealership's own acquisition needs), this automation runs a monthly scan of past customers' vehicles on file and identifies anyone whose trade-in value has risen meaningfully since their last visit or purchase.

Those customers receive a personalized text or email with an actual estimated trade-in offer for their specific vehicle, not a generic "we want your car" message, along with a link to schedule an appraisal.

Customers sitting on a vehicle worth more than they realize get a concrete reason to come back in, and the dealership fills its used inventory pipeline with qualified trade-in leads instead of relying only on walk-ins.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, an used car manager spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.
tools: vAuto or Black Book (market valuation data)

automations.title: Digital Vehicle Inspection Delivery
automations.summary: As soon as a technician completes a multi-point inspection using a tablet-based digital inspection tool, photos and short video clips of any flagged…
steps: As soon as a technician completes a multi-point inspection using a tablet-based digital inspection tool, photos and short video clips of any flagged issues (worn brake pads, a cracked belt, low tread depth) are automatically compiled with the technician's written notes into a single report and texted to the customer while the vehicle is still on the lift.
Customers see exactly what the technician saw instead of taking a stranger's word for it over the phone, and they can approve or decline each recommended repair directly from the report.

Approval rates on recommended work climb because customers are looking at their own worn brake pads instead of a verbal description, and the service advisor spends less time explaining and more time closing.
automations.manualProcess: The manual approach means a shop foreman handles each case reactively, after someone has already noticed something went wrong.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Tekmetric or Shop-Ware)
AutoVitals or Bolt On (digital inspection app)

automations.title: Invoice-Triggered Review Request
automations.summary: The moment a repair invoice is marked paid in the shop management system, this automation waits roughly two hours (enough time for the customer to…
steps: The moment a repair invoice is marked paid in the shop management system, this automation waits roughly two hours (enough time for the customer to drive away and settle in, not so long the visit feels distant) before sending a text asking for a quick Google review, with a direct link that drops the customer straight into the review form.

Customers who report a low satisfaction score in the initial quick-rating question are routed privately to the shop owner instead of being pushed toward a public review, catching problems before they turn into a bad post.

Review volume grows on a predictable weekly cadence instead of depending on the rare customer who thinks to leave one unprompted, and the shop builds a public track record it can point to when competing for new customers.

steps: Customers automatically receive a reminder text or email the day before their scheduled service appointment and again the morning of, including drop-off instructions, the estimated service time, and a link to reschedule if the timing no longer works.
Appointments that go unconfirmed after the second reminder are automatically flagged to the service coordinator so a quick phone call can catch a no-show before the bay sits empty.

Shops running this sequence consistently see fewer missed appointments and a smoother morning drop-off line, since customers arrive already knowing what to expect instead of showing up unsure why they're there.

The fixed ops director gets a weekly count of vehicles due that haven't yet booked, giving the service department a ready list to call instead of waiting for customers to remember on their own.
Open recalls in particular get caught and resolved faster, closing a safety and liability gap that used to depend entirely on a customer noticing a mailed notice.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a fixed ops director is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background.

Approvals captured by text flow straight back into the repair order, so the technician can start additional work within minutes instead of the car sitting untouched while a service advisor tries to reach the customer by phone.

steps: A customer who starts but doesn't finish an online credit application automatically triggers a follow-up within the hour offering help completing it, either by text with a direct link back to the saved form or a call from a credit analyst, instead of the abandoned application simply vanishing into an analytics report nobody checks.
Abandonment points are tracked automatically, so if customers consistently stall on the same field, income verification, for example, that friction point gets flagged for the finance team to fix.

The service scheduler sees a far more accurate due list than one built purely on time-based rules, and customers get reminders that actually match how they use their vehicle instead of a generic date that either arrives too early or, worse, too late.
automations.manualProcess: Manually, a service scheduler is stuck doing repetitive follow-ups and data entry that could otherwise run quietly in the background. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

automations.title: Body Shop Estimate & Insurance Claims Coordination
automations.summary: Once a repair estimate is prepared in the body shop, it's automatically sent to the customer for review and, at the same time, submitted directly to…
steps: Once a repair estimate is prepared in the body shop, it's automatically sent to the customer for review and, at the same time, submitted directly to their insurance claims adjuster, cutting out the delay that used to come from a body shop manager manually faxing or emailing the same estimate to two separate parties on two separate timelines.

Adjuster approvals and any requested revisions flow back into the same estimate automatically, so a supplement doesn't sit waiting in an inbox, and the whole approval cycle that used to take several days routinely closes within one.
automations.manualProcess: Without this system, a body shop manager manually pieces together information from different places, then has to relay it to everyone who needs it. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
tools: Shop management software (e.g., Tekmetric or Shop-Ware)

steps: When the new model year of a vehicle a past customer already owns is unveiled, that customer automatically receives an announcement highlighting what's new, paired with a trade-in incentive designed to bring them back in before the current model year's residual value starts to slide.

The dealership sales manager gets a report of which past customers responded and booked a visit, sharpening which model refreshes are actually worth a dedicated campaign versus a generic mass email, and this single automated trigger consistently surfaces upgrade-ready customers who weren't actively shopping until the message reminded them the new version existed.
automations.manualProcess: The manual version of this puts the entire workload on a dealership sales manager, who has to juggle phone calls, emails, and spreadsheets just to keep things moving. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

steps: When a repair estimate indicates a turnaround long enough to require a rental, the automation automatically flags the job and coordinates a rental car arrangement with the customer ahead of drop-off, confirming pickup timing and coverage details before the customer arrives without a way home.

The rental coordinator no longer has to manually cross-reference every open repair order against expected completion time to catch which customers will need a rental, since the system flags it automatically the moment an estimate crosses the threshold, and customers show up already knowing a rental is arranged instead of being surprised by the news at the counter.
automations.manualProcess: Without automation, this falls entirely on a rental coordinator, who has to track every step by hand across emails, spreadsheets, and sticky notes. It rarely feels urgent in the moment, but it adds up fast.

steps: Right after a vehicle purchase closes, the new owner is automatically introduced to the service department by name, with their first maintenance visit pre-scheduled at the standard interval, smoothing the handoff between the sales floor and the service drive that too often leaves a new owner without a single point of contact once the deal is signed.

The service advisor assigned to that customer gets advance notice of the new relationship before the customer ever calls in, and dealerships tracking this handoff see meaningfully higher service retention among new owners compared to customers left to find the service department on their own.
automations.manualProcess: Done manually, a service advisor has to remember to follow up on every case individually, often relying on memory, phone calls, and whatever notes didn't get lost. Over a month, those small manual steps add up to a significant amount of lost time.

Advisors can see how their own numbers stack up, and a director walks into a coaching conversation with actual data on which specific service, which specific advisor, is underperforming, turning a vague sense that "upsells feel low lately" into a targeted, effective coaching plan.
automations.manualProcess: Handled by hand, a fixed ops director spends time each day re-checking the same information across disconnected tools instead of doing higher-value work. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.

Customers who get a well-timed reminder before a deferred repair turns into a breakdown are far more likely to come back and complete the work on their own schedule instead of an emergency one, and the shop recovers a meaningful share of revenue that used to be declined and forgotten permanently.

A fast, thoughtful response to both positive and negative reviews is one of the strongest signals shoppers use to judge a dealership before ever walking in, and consistent response time, not just eventual response, is what separates dealerships that manage their reputation actively from ones that only react.
automations.manualProcess: Done by hand, this depends entirely on a reputation specialist remembering to check in, update records, and follow up, with no safety net if something slips. It's the kind of work that quietly eats hours every week.
